how_to_use: 1. Pick stacks from the JD (react, vue, node, java, cloud). Any combination works. The stack the JD stresses first is the PRIMARY stack.
2. INCLUDE: for each skill, it is included when (a) the JD names it (its name or any alias, case-insensitive, whole words), OR (b) its 'include' condition is true. Then 'exclude' removes it if true.
include may be: true (always), false (only when the JD names it), or a condition object.

3. CONDITIONS (one operator per object, combine with all/any/not): { stack: [..] } any of these stacks picked | { notStack: [..] } none picked | { named: [..] } any of these skills named in the JD | { namedAll: [..] } all named | { notNamed: [..] } none named | { all: [..] } | { any: [..] } | { not: cond }.
4. rank: 'related' lists the skill after core skills in its category; default is core. A skill named in the JD always sorts first.

5. requires: including a skill also includes each listed prerequisite, recursively, even if that prerequisite is not otherwise included. Same-category prerequisites are listed before the skill that needs them; a skill included only as a prerequisite goes at the end of its category.

6. pulls: if a skill is NAMED in the JD, the listed skills are also included and listed after it, recursively (React named pulls Next.js and Redux; Vue named pulls Nuxt.js and Pinia). Merely picking the stack does not trigger it.
7. exclude (condition): drops the skill after everything else. moveTo: [{ when: cond, category }] moves an included skill into another source category (first match wins).

8. GROUPS: skills keep their source 'categories'; the resume shows the groups in 'outputGroups' (max 9). A group holds its sources one after another; empty groups are dropped. Group order = groupOrder[primary stack]. promoteGroup: if react or vue is picked, 'Frontend & UI' goes directly after Languages.
9. SKILL ORDER inside a category: same-category prerequisite first; otherwise JD-named skills, then core, then related, ties in file order; prerequisite-only skills last.
10. Only include skills the candidate really has. If the JD asks for a skill not listed here, do not invent it.
11. 'why' is a human note explaining an exception; the code ignores it.
